datePolicy.dateRangeRule: When a source describes an event as a date range, create or expand records for every calendar day inside the range. Prefer one event record per active day unless the source clearly describes a single overnight event.
datePolicy.deletionRule: Do not delete historical events during refresh. Do not remove future events only because they disappeared from a listing page.
datePolicy.cancelRule: Mark an event cancelled only when the official source explicitly says it is cancelled.

eligibilityPolicy.defaultRule: Keep events that children can reasonably attend or that are family-compatible, even when the event is not exclusively for children.
eligibilityPolicy.grayAreaRule: Keep gray-area community events unless the event is clearly adult-only, unsafe, or inappropriate for children.
grayAreaExamplesToKeep: community health or safety events with family participation
excludeSignals: beer garden as the primary activity
adult nightlife, club, DJ, drag party, or bar/brewery party events when they run late or overnight
yard sale, garage sale, rummage sale, estate sale, tag sale, moving sale, flea market, swap meet, or free market
secondhand sale or exchange events whose primary activity is browsing, donating, buying, selling, or swapping used items
broad festival, series, season, or umbrella listing cards that do not identify a specific activity, performer/program, or kid/family-compatible content
location-only summaries such as a city name, venue group, various locations, or multiple city names when paired with a generic festival or series title
events starting at 10 PM or later unless explicitly reviewed
overnight or midnight events when the source explicitly lists a midnight/early-morning start time
explicitly unsafe or inappropriate for children
eligibilityPolicy.exclusionRule: Exclude only when children clearly cannot attend or the event is clearly not suitable for children. Municipal adult/senior programming such as chair yoga, senior-center movie days, adult wellness classes, and senior camp/social activities should not be imported even when the title contains otherwise kid-compatible words such as yoga, movie, or camp.
eligibilityPolicy.timeExclusionRule: Exclude events that start at 10 PM or later. Also exclude adult nightlife, club, DJ, drag-party, bar, brewery, or similar late/overnight social events when the content is clearly not kid-appropriate, even if the source tags them as family/community. Do not automatically exclude 9 PM community events such as fireworks or public watch parties; keep them only when children can reasonably attend. For 12 AM-4:59 AM starts, exclude only when the source explicitly gives an overnight/midnight/early-morning time, because some sources use 00:00 as a date-only placeholder.

eventSchemaGuidance.townAssignmentRule: Every event should ultimately have event.townId set to the town where the event physically happens. Statewide, regional, county, tourism, directory, and carnival sources must still assign each event by its venue/address town, not by the source service area. If the address town is not already in data/event-sources.json towns, do not auto-create a town; keep townId null, preserve the raw address/locality, set townAssignmentStatus to needs_registry_town, and leave the event for review until the user decides whether to add that town. Do not assign townId from a source organization's office address or placeholder venue name such as Visit Somerset NJ Events; assign only from the actual event venue/address, or leave townId empty with an explicit review status.
eventSchemaGuidance.summaryRule: Summary should contain activity content only. Do not put date, time, venue, room, place, or address text in summary. If a summary is only a city, town, venue, address, room, or other location label, treat it as missing activity content; do not publish broad festival, series, season, or umbrella listing cards unless the title or details identify a specific child/family-compatible activity.
eventSchemaGuidance.placeDisplayRule: venueName should be a human-readable place or venue name, not just a street address, intersection, vague area, route, or source placeholder. If a source location field is only a street address and the source registry has a confirmed venue/library name, use the confirmed name for venueName and keep the street address in address. If the source gives a place-like display name without a full address, such as a gazebo, bandstand, field, playground, pavilion, plaza, or named room, reverse-look up that display name with the town/venue context and use the resolved address or coordinates for navigation; mark addressLookupSource as place_name_reverse_lookup when practical. If the lookup is likely but not official, keep the useful address, mark addressStatus approximate or needs_review, and preserve the display name in venueName instead of falling back to a generic municipal default. If an event is genuinely spread across downtown, a route, or multiple sites, keep the broad place name only; use addressStatus area_confirmed when the area/route is confirmed but there is no single precise navigation point, otherwise use addressStatus approximate or needs_review and reviewNotes explaining the uncertainty.
eventSchemaGuidance.sourceUrlRule: Keep the original official event page when available. If only a calendar listing exists, keep that listing URL. When the same activity has multiple source pages, the app should display only one source link: prefer the official organizer, venue, municipal, library, or program detail page; use discovery, directory, ticketing, or reposted pages such as Patch or Eventbrite only when no official page is available. Extra evidence links may stay in source data for review, but the visible app button should remain a single Source page.
eventSchemaGuidance.duplicateRule: Treat events as strong duplicates when normalized titles match or are near-identical, dates match, start times match, and the town/venue/source context points to the same activity, even when sourceId or venue wording differs. Prefer the record with the most specific confirmed venue/address, end time, source URL, and useful kid/family summary. Source priority is organizer/venue official pages, then municipal/library/county tourism reposts, then ticketing pages, then third-party directories such as Patch or NJ Carnivals. If an official or municipal record is only a placeholder, has a vague venue, wrong/default address, or empty summary, keep the more accurate third-party record and mark reviewNotes. Do not use same venue plus same start time alone as a duplicate signal when one record may be an umbrella program and another is a specific sub-activity.
eventSchemaGuidance.evidenceRule: Manual or configured events should keep evidenceUrl, evidenceType, and checkedAt when practical.
eventSchemaGuidance.dateExpansionRule: For multi-day listings, keep each active day visible in data/events.json. If the source gives a continuous range but no per-day schedule, repeat the best-known title/source/venue details for each date and mark dateStatus as inferred_range or dateExpansionStatus as needs_review when the active days are not certain. If an event title or URL explicitly contains an older calendar date for the same month/day than the structured future startsAt date, treat it as a stale old event and exclude it instead of rolling it forward.
eventSchemaGuidance.allDayTimeRule: If a source says all day, look up the venue/source operating hours for that date and use those hours only when they are official and date-specific enough. When official venue hours are confirmed, replace All day with the venue's open-to-close hours for that date and mark timeStatus as official_venue_hours. If the venue is confirmed closed on that date, keep the row out of the app until confirmed. If exact hours cannot be confirmed, do not guess; leave startsAt/endsAt time components or time empty as appropriate, use Date listed; time TBA when the source is really date-only, and mark timeStatus as date_only_time_unconfirmed or needs_review. If a structured source uses 00:00 through 23:59/24:00 as an all-day range, do not show 12:00 AM - 11:59 PM.
eventSchemaGuidance.addressLookupRule: If an event gives a venue but no address, search the official venue/source page first, then reliable map or directory sources for the exact street address. If the exact address cannot be found, leave address blank rather than guessing; if only a likely or approximate place is known, mark addressStatus as approximate or needs_review and lower confidence.
eventSchemaGuidance.coordinateAccuracyRule: Coordinate priority is strict: first use coordinates supplied by the event source or confirmed source registry location; if no coordinates are supplied but a specific street address exists, geocode that address; only when neither source coordinates nor a usable address exists may an event fall back to the town center. Town-center fallback records must set coordinateStatus to town_center_fallback, set directionsDisabled true, and mark addressStatus needs_review or area_confirmed as appropriate. When an event has a specific street address, lat/lng must represent that address or a confirmed entrance/venue point for that same place. Do not reuse a town center, source office, parser default, or unrelated venue coordinate for a specific event address. If a configured source, regional source, municipal source, or shared calendar emits the same exact coordinate for multiple different street addresses or venues, treat those coordinates as suspicious: geocode the specific address, use official venue coordinates when available, or mark addressStatus/coordinateStatus as needs_review and leave coordinates empty rather than publishing a misleading pin.
eventSchemaGuidance.uncertaintyRule: Prefer accurate empty fields plus explicit status markers over guessed data. Use status review, confidence below the normal source confidence, and field-level markers such as dateStatus, timeStatus, addressStatus, townAssignmentStatus, summaryStatus, or reviewNotes whenever a value is inferred, missing, image-derived, or uncertain.

eventStatuses.review: Event is useful but has incomplete or uncertain fields.
eventStatuses.cancelled: Official source explicitly says the event is cancelled.
eventStatuses.stale_possible: Future event was previously seen but no longer appears on the source; not enough evidence to cancel.
eventStatuses.duplicate: Event was merged into a better canonical record.

confidenceGuidance.meaning: Official API or structured official detail page with complete fields.
Official page with some inferred or cleaned fields.
Official flyer, manual transcription, or configured source with enough evidence.
Third-party directory or incomplete source; keep only if useful and mark for review.

qualityChecks: Every real event should have a stable id and sourceId.
Every real event should ultimately have a townId for its physical event location.
If the physical town is not in the registry yet, keep the event in review/pending town assignment rather than auto-adding a town.
Every real event should have a sourceUrl or url back to the source.
Every displayed map event should have coordinates or a geocodable address.
Do not invent activity descriptions when the source does not provide one.
Check visible-date duplicates by normalized title, date, start time, source URL, venue/address, and cross-source reposts; merge into the best canonical record rather than publishing parallel copies.

Broad festival, series, season, or umbrella listings must identify a specific activity, performer/program, or kid/family-compatible content before publishing; location-only summaries are insufficient.
Prefer official HTML text before image, flyer, or OCR text.
Use image or flyer text only when normal page text is missing needed date, time, room, address, or venue detail.
For date ranges, verify that every date in the range has a record or an explicit review marker explaining why daily expansion was not possible.
For all-day events, verify official operating hours before filling exact times; otherwise leave the exact time blank and mark the uncertainty.
For missing addresses, search official venue/source pages and reliable references before leaving address blank or marking it approximate.
Any field that was inferred from weak evidence, image text, or judgment should be marked so accuracy-based manual review can find it.
